entries.title: Android <= 12 CoC data loss under congestion
entries.behaviour: Forwarding LE CoC writers (call relays, stream relays and forwarders, and a helper's parent link once it becomes a relay hop) write SDUs of up to 8,000 bytes (within the peer's receive limit) instead of 245-byte single-PDU SDUs, so the SDU-counted L2CAP queue stays below its congestion quota for the same bytes; nothing is paced or dropped and endpoint links are unchanged. Before Android 13 btif_sock_thread could read stale poll entries while several sockets were busy and drop data read from a socket whose channel was congested. A 'Secure link decrypt failed' or record-sequence failure on a hop from such a forwarder is a candidate stack data loss (the hop_integrity line tells a shifted stream from a changed byte). DEBUG test_relay_coc_coalesce=true applies it where this matcher holds.

entries.behaviour: Mark the test_gatt_request_mtu experiment as not applicable when either phone runs API 34+ (the stack requests 517 for the first client and ignores later requests) and log the negotiated MTU instead. entries.title: LE scan start quota (5 starts per 30 s)
effects: at most 5 BLE scan starts per 30 s (a further start waits instead of being refused)
entries.behaviour: Every BLE scan start (including the low-latency -> balanced switch) takes a slot from a budget of 5 per rolling 30 s. A balanced switch without a free slot keeps the low-latency scan (no queued restart), so slots stay free for new discovery such as calls. The stack counts per app UID in the Bluetooth process, so the count survives our process restarts: starts are persisted (elapsedRealtime) and seed the gate at process start, keyed by Settings.Global.BOOT_COUNT so a reboot never seeds stale starts.

entries.title: Retry LE connect failures beyond status 133
effects: retry GATT connection-stage failures with status [8, 34, 62, 133, 147]

entries.title: Exynos 9611 relay: a central child link at the parent's interval can get no events at all
entries.behaviour: Proposal (diagnostic): a relay on this controller (peripheral to its parent, central to its child, both HIGH = 15 ms) loses its child link in about half of the attempts: 22 of 55 never established (HCI 0x3E), 9 went silent for 5.0-5.1 s after the update to 15 ms (0x08; in the four diag cases the last completed packet came 77-92 ms after the update), the rest ran starved or healthy. Every M31 15 ms stage with the child anchor 11.3-13.7 ms after the parent anchor was dead or starved (8 of 8); every one at 3.7-10.3 ms was healthy except two CoC stages without a data-length update (6.1/6.6 ms, 17-29 kbps). The generic mitigations (relay_child_stall_guard, relay_child_reanchor, relay_establish_fallback) apply to every phone; a child that is an A15s (MediaTek MT6765, Android 10) fails alike (11 of 23 attempts, 2026-10-12): six of nine failed attempts left the child with no connect request at all, three left both ends connected with no first anchor, and direct M31->A15s without a parent link lost about 2 of 28. The Experimental test_relay_establish_budget retries these fast 0x3E failures in place for 12 s. This entry only records the family so a later A/B (test_relay_upstream_dck, test_gatt_request_mtu) can promote a family-specific rule, for example a 30 ms parent link or a smaller data length for a relay child on this controller.

sources.note: the stack locks 7.5 ms connection parameters while GATT service discovery runs and applies the app's pending request when it ends; every central here shows 45 -> 7.5 -> 15 ms (the HIGH range 11.25-15 ms resolves to 15 ms on the Exynos, Qualcomm and S24 controllers seen)

gatt_high_priority_min/max_interval 9/12 (11.25-15 ms), gatt_balanced 24/40 (30-50 ms), gatt_dck_priority 24/24 (30 ms); the app cannot ask for another interval (hidden BluetoothGatt.requestLeConnectionUpdate throws NoSuchMethodException, relaylink-arms2r1)

Lower the BLE connection supervision timeout to 5s (2017): every requestConnectionPriority sends timeout = 500 (5 s) on Android 10+ (20 s on 8-9), so the '0x08 after 5.0-5.1 s of silence' above is this timer expiring, not a stack fault (aosp-bt-versions CONN-01); the link-silence line now names it

Nordic's controller (a different vendor): peripheral link timing is dictated by the peer central and may collide with any running event; central link events are placed relative to other central links only; a lower-priority event is blocked and rescheduled, and a peripheral connection about to time out gets the highest priority. The Exynos 9611 controller shows no such rescue (0x08 after 5.0 s of silence)

Core Vol 6 Part B 4.5 (connection state: events, supervision timer) and 5.1.1 (connection update: transmit window): two connections' overlapping events are left to the controller; no Samsung or Exynos document describes its scheduler

entries.title: Android 14 and earlier: a BluetoothGatt that returned busy once can stay busy for ever (Experimental arm: applied only with test_gatt_busy_wedge=recover)
effects: busy write with nothing in flight = wedged client: end the link at once; with another local holder retry every 25 ms up to 500 ms
entries.behaviour: MeshLive tracks its own outstanding write on each GATT client. A busy answer (201 on Android 13-14, a bare false before API 33) while it has none in flight is not its own flag: the framework already retried 5 x 10 ms, so the client object is stuck (mDeviceBusy never cleared, or the per-peer write permit leaked by a client that disconnected mid-write). The 2 ms x 500 ms spin cannot succeed then. The link is ended at once with a distinct failure, the client is closed, and the next connect to that peer waits for the ACL to drop (up to 2 s) so a new client does not inherit the stuck permit. When the registry shows another local client to the same peer (a real second holder of the permit) the write is still retried for up to 500 ms, now every 25 ms. ROOT REVIEW: this ends a link on ONE busy answer on SDK 33-34 without phone evidence, so it is applied only with test_gatt_busy_wedge=recover (DEBUG, Experimental); the shipped default is legacy, the old 2 ms spin.

effects: after a client connects, a PHY read unanswered for 400 ms means the stack lost the server's connection record: cancel the connection and register the server again
after a client subscribed, no data write for 1200 ms means the stack drops this connection's writes before the app: cancel the connection and register the server again (never after any data arrived)

a re-registration replaces only the GATT server and keeps the running advertising set (same address); after a subscribe the set stays on until the first data write; a rotating-ID epoch change always stops it
entries.behaviour: After a client connects to the advertising call listener, the server reads the link's PHY; a healthy stack answers in 5-10 ms. When no PHY answer comes within 400 ms the stack has no record of this connection for the server, so every response would go to connection 0 and the client's subscribe would hang to its timeout: the server logs gatt_server_connection_untracked, cancels the connection and registers itself again (close, open, add the service, advertise). The client's retry then reaches a freshly registered server. Only the advertising listener is watched (the dual-listening second server also hears links it does not own). Newer stacks may never call back a PHY read (AdaptivePhy's Android 13 backstop), so the watch is limited to the legacy stack. Second stage: after the client's subscribe is accepted, its first data write must reach the app within 1.2 s (healthy first writes arrive 70-140 ms later); otherwise the server logs gatt_server_first_write_missing, ends that connection and registers again. A connection that has delivered any data is never cut. A re-registration replaces only the GATT server: the advertising set is a separate stack object, so a running set keeps advertising with the same address and the client's retry finds it at once; to keep it for stage 2 the set stays on after the subscribe until the first data write (at most the 1.2 s watch) instead of stopping at the subscribe. A rotating-ID epoch change always stops the set, so an address never carries into a new epoch.

sources.note: onClientConnected: the connection is added to mServerMap only when getById(serverIf) finds the server
serverReadPhy: connIdByAddress(serverIf, address) null -> 'no connection to <address>', nothing is read
sendResponse: a missing connection is sent as connId 0 (the stack then rejects it: gatt_if out of range)

onServerWriteCharacteristic: a write that reached the stack is dropped silently when mHandleMap.getByHandle or mServerMap.getById finds no entry (stage 2: the first handshake write never reaches the app)

entries.fallback: The client's subscribe waits for its 12 s timeout and retries; the retry reaches a fresh server only when the listener was rebuilt for another reason.
evidence: benchmarks/runs/edgecases-20261020 (asus-s22-fb0e, s22-asus-r3..r6, asus-s22-r3..r6) and benchmarks/runs/longcall-035b5235-20261020 (lc-s22-asus-r3..r5), ASUS (Android 11, legacy stack) called by the S22: 16 of 16 failed first connects reached a server idle for more than 10 s: 'serverReadPhy() - no connection to <addr>' 8 ms after onClientConnected, then 'address not found for given connId' and a failed CCCD sendResponse (gatt_if out of range = 0); the client's subscribe hung to its 12 s timeout. 16 of 16 retries on freshly registered servers worked. No failure before about 02:17; the onset followed a rising count of other apps' GATT registrations without callbacks (5 to 9).

benchmarks/runs/edgecases-20261020/asus-a15s-m31-055022 step 2 (A15s calling the ASUS back, server registered 16 s earlier): the PHY read was answered and the subscribe acknowledged; the A15s's first 133-byte handshake write reached the ASUS stack (gatt_data_process op_code=82) but never the app (bmh3 responder EOFException after 4692 ms); the A15s's setup-stall guard closed at 3.0 s, and the retry after rediscovery worked in 211 ms.
entries.confidence_note: Symptom and recovery measured 16/16 on one Android 11 phone; why the stack loses the record is not proven (the server map lookup is the documented path). Other legacy-stack phones: not measured.

entries.title: Foreground service start failures are caught and reported
effects: catch a refused foreground-service start; fall back to the connectedDevice type and report it
entries.behaviour: Only Android's two refusals are handled: a background start (ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException) or a while-in-use camera/microphone type refusal (SecurityException '... foreground only permission'). Manifest bugs (Invalid/MissingForegroundServiceType, other SecurityException) still propagate.

entries.behaviour: The stack raises the LE link-layer data length (up to 251 bytes) only after an ATT MTU exchange; an L2CAP CoC channel alone does not, until Android 16 QPR1 sets the data length on a CoC connect. On the fresh-ACL CoC client (the GATT client is closed before the CoC connect) the arm opens one short GATT client on the new ACL right after the CoC connect, requests MTU 517, waits for onMtuChanged, closes it and logs BENCHMARK coc_mtu_prime (requested and effective MTU, inferred data length) before the normal GATT attach and any CoC traffic. Default ON on the stacks where this client path runs (Android 12-13, entry le-coc-eatt-stranded-channels); elsewhere the control GATT client stays open and already exchanged the MTU, and a skipped line with reason=control-link-alive is logged. entries.title: The advertising-set budget is learned from start refusals; optional sets yield

entries.behaviour: The number of advertising instances is whatever the controller reports (the CDD only says SHOULD 4, a cheap controller can offer one) and every app and the system share it, so it cannot be read. MeshLive learns it: a refusal with TOO_MANY_ADVERTISERS while it owns n sets means the budget is n now (kept five minutes). With a short budget the reach and title sets do not start (they need one instance plus one spare), and a refused session-critical set (the stream's own advertisement) first stops the title set, then the reach set, waits for the stack to confirm the stop (the instance is freed asynchronously) and retries once. Priority: stable offer > reach > title > probe. Starts also wait up to 0.7 s for stops still in flight. No advertisement changes. Off: previous behaviour (probe-only gating, no preemption, no stop wait).

entries.title: One link-layer procedure in flight per LE link (MTU, PHY, connection update)
entries.behaviour: Proposal (Experimental, test_ll_gate=true): requestMtu, discoverServices, setPreferredPhy and requestConnectionPriority on one link are queued through LlProcedureGate: one in flight, a settle gap after each (400 ms after MTU, 1.5 s after a PHY update, 750 ms after a connection update), a peripheral sends no PHY request before the central's first connection update plus three intervals and its service discovery, a PHY answered with 0x23/0x2A is retried once on 1M, a missing callback is bounded and not stacked on, and a link lost within 5 s of a PHY update stays on 1M for that peer. Costs a few seconds before 2M. Off: every request goes straight to the stack, as it does today.

sources.reference: Bluetooth Core Specification v5.4 Vol 6 Part B 5.3 (procedure collisions)
sources.note: two instant-based procedures (connection update, PHY update) may not be pending together; the second is rejected with 0x23 LL procedure collision or 0x2A different transaction collision
Zephyr: "certain phones in the market perform Connection Update Procedure and do not correctly handle remote initiated colliding PHY update procedures" (2018-08-17)

Nordic engineer: Galaxy S21 answers LL_PHY_REQ immediately instead of waiting for LL_CONNECTION_UPDATE_IND; Broadcom fixed the controller bug, Samsung had not shipped it (a forum claim, no official source)
Lenovo M10: disconnect 0x2A within 5 s of the 2M update; fixed by disabling the auto PHY update or delaying it

the stack locks 7.5 ms parameters while service discovery runs and applies the app's request afterwards; AOSP does not serialise the app's PHY, MTU/DLE and priority requests (serialised only in Android 16)

entries.fallback: Requests are issued as today; LeConnectionPriorityKeeper retries a failed connection update.
evidence: none: status 42 "BLE PHY unavailable" collisions seen on M31, ASUS and A15s in 2026-10-07 runs led to commit 2cbdafb1; no retained run isolates the gate
entries.confidence_note: The spec rule and the error codes are primary; the Broadcom/Samsung attribution is a Nordic engineer's forum statement, and the default behaviour is already measured on six phones, so the gate stays an A/B arm.

entries.title: Roll back the last MTU, PHY or priority change after a link is lost within 10 s of it
entries.behaviour: Proposal (Experimental, test_link_change_rollback=true): a link lost with a fault status (0x08, 0x22, 0x23, 0x2A, 0x3E, 133, 147) within 10 s of an MTU, PHY or priority change remembers that change as bad for the peer; the next connection asks for MTU 185, stays on 1M, or asks for BALANCED. The memory expires on a Bluetooth restart, a security-patch change or after 7 days. Off: no memory, the existing 2M->1M adaptive memory is unchanged.

disconnect 0x2A shortly after a PHY change on a Lenovo M10

entries.title: Request the connection priority again when the interval reverts to the default
entries.behaviour: Proposal (Experimental, test_priority_reassert=true): when onConnectionUpdated reports an interval above the requested priority's maximum (HIGH asks 11.25-15 ms and the link falls back to 45 ms), the same priority is requested again after 1 s and 3 s, at most twice, and not when the second report shows the same interval (a floor such as the 20 ms hearing-aid minimum). Off: the drift is only logged.

the interval flips back to 30 ms after CONNECTION_PRIORITY_HIGH was requested
a request issued while another update is pending is dropped (one slot, the later request replaces the earlier); the stack applies the queued request when service discovery ends

entries.title: Treat Coded PHY as active only when the stack reported it
entries.behaviour: Proposal (needs the LinkCapacity/LinkSelfMeasurement call sites to pass trustedExperimentalPhy): the Coded pacer prior and capacity key apply only after a PHY callback with status 0 reported Coded; an unconfirmed Coded request is treated as the PHY the link really runs on. Connections stay on LE 1M first and Coded is requested after connect; Coded-primary scanning is not used (impossible before Android 15), and 1M is always in the connectGatt mask.

setPreferredPhy requests a PHY; onPhyUpdate reports the result and the stack may keep the current PHY
